ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the main path from left to right is that the input R(s) first passes through an integration block labeled 1/s, and then enters the first summing node; the output of the first summing node then passes through the second integration block labeled 1/s, then enters the second summing node, and finally the output is C(s). In the lower part of the figure there is a horizontal branch split from the input R(s), which connects upward respectively into the first summing node and the second summing node; both connection ports are marked with plus signs. Therefore the lower branch is a feedforward branch from R(s) to the two summing nodes, not a feedback branch returning from C(s). Reasoning calculation: Let the input be R(s). After passing through the first integrator, the signal is R(s)/s. The first summing node adds this signal and the directly feedforward R(s) from below, so the output of the first summing node is R(s)/s + R(s). After this signal passes through the second integrator, it becomes (R(s)/s + R(s))/s = R(s)/s^2 + R(s)/s. The second summing node then adds the directly feedforward R(s) from below, so C(s)=R(s)/s^2 + R(s)/s + R(s). Dividing both sides by R(s), obtain C(s)/R(s)=1/s^2+1/s+1=(s^2+s+1)/s^2.
